julia.docs: heads-up — i'm holding PR #4123 (link below) until runtime confirms the default behavior on model-fallback when streaming is enabled. docs preview showing behavior that might be misleading. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4123
ci-bot: docs-preview: failed — snapshot mismatch on /api-reference/generate (preview build 782) :warning:
ben.runtime: can you paste the minimal repro? is this about the SDK streaming param falling back to non-streaming model? :eyes:
julia.docs: short repro i used in the examples section:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-tuned-llama","input":"hello","stream":true}'
```
response in preview shows a single complete JSON chunk (no SSE) and README text says: "If stream=true we will stream tokens; otherwise full response." — that's what triggered me.
kevin: hmm. runtime note: we have fallback routing that can switch to a compatible model variant which may not support streaming; default should be to preserve stream semantics and fall back to a non-streaming response only if the customer has fallback_on_error=true in their route config.
sasha.docs: do we have that config listed in the docs? i couldn't find fallback_on_error in the public API reference, only in the dedicated config guide.
ben.runtime: confirming — the platform behavior is: by default we DO NOT silently degrade stream -> non-stream. two cases: 1) if primary model errors mid-stream and route has fallback_on_error=true then we attempt fallback (non-streaming) and return final chunk; 2) without fallback_on_error we return the error and the stream closes. i can add an authoritative note.
julia.docs: ok that's helpful. so the docs should say: "streaming requests are NOT implicitly converted to non-streaming; explicit fallback_on_error is required to auto-switch."
tara.ml: also note an edge case: tiny model variants may accept stream param but buffer internally and flush whole output at once for short responses — that's an implementation detail, we should call it out as "model-variant buffering may cause single-chunk response even when streaming is enabled" to avoid confusion.
kevin: @ben.runtime can you paste the exact config key and default (true/false) so we can update the reference and the migration guide?
ben.runtime: sure — key is `route.fallback_on_error` default: `false`. rollout note: teams can set `fallback_on_error: true` at route-level or via runtime policy to enable transparent fallbacks. i'll add a short snippet for the docs.
sasha.docs: perfect. i'll update PR #4123 to include the clarification, add the config reference and an example warning about buffering and fallback semantics.
julia.docs: assigning reviewers: @kevin, @tara (please review once i push the patch). holding merge until ben's snippet + a CI preview rebuild passes. :thumbsup:
devops-bot: preview rebuild triggered for PR 4123 (build 783). logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/783 :robot_face:
ci-bot: docs-preview: success (build 783) :tada:
kevin: looks good to me, added :eyes: on wording.
tara.ml: fine from ML side, small nit on phrasing.
julia.docs: merging after squash. thanks everyone. :party:
